page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs (64 physical cores) utilizing Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 4096.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of a 3800 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a Passmark CPU score in the top 10% (85629.49) and strong multi-core stress-ng performance. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 302.32 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations. Cryptographic execution is also notable, with the Passmark CPU encryption test placing in the top 10%. However, while prompt processing for medium LLM models is strong, text generation for large 70B LLM models is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25% at 2.76 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

Given its massive memory footprint and high-speed local NVMe storage, the x2iedn.32xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, big data analytics, and memory-intensive simulation tasks. The inclusion of local NVMe SSDs and 100 Gbps networking ensures low-latency data access and rapid node-to-node communication in clustered environments.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, it features 128 vCPUs from Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz, paired with 4096.0 GB of DDR4 RAM and 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance delivers 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results show top-tier performance in Passmark CPU and encryption tests, alongside strong memory bandwidth of 302.32 GB/sec for large blocks. While CPU-based cryptographic and database operations are highly efficient, the lack of dedicated GPUs limits its utility for large-scale LLM text generation. This instance is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy caching layers, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
